headline: Bitcoin slips below $80K as Fed meeting opens and Ripple wins national bank charter
summary: Bitcoin dipped under $80,000 for the first time in recent sessions, brushing off a positive Asian tech rally as traders turned their attention to the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting that kicked off today. The bigger story may be regulatory: Ripple secured final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) for a national trust bank charter, placing its RLUSD stablecoin under federal oversight — a landmark for institutional crypto credibility. Zcash was the day's standout mover, gaining 2.35% after a co-founder proposed ending the project's grants program and pointing to a $125 million treasury.

winners.name: Zcash
winners.catalyst: Zcash co-founder proposed ending the project's grants funding program, citing a $125 million treasury balance. The proposal drew attention to Zcash's substantial reserves and sparked speculation about capital redistribution, driving the day's outperformance.

losers.name: Rain
losers.catalyst: No clear catalyst identified — the move appears to reflect technical selling pressure or thin liquidity rather than a specific news event.

whyItMoved:
The dominant force today was the opening of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting, which pulled trader attention away from broader risk assets. Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 — a psychologically significant level — even as Asian tech stocks rallied, a decoupling that signals crypto markets are pricing in Fed uncertainty rather than following the usual risk-on playbook. The Fear & Greed index sits at 48, squarely in neutral territory, consistent with a market that is waiting rather than acting.

Solana was the hardest hit among large caps, falling 1.28% to $100.11, though no specific catalyst drove the move beyond the broader cautious tone. XRP bucked the trend with a 0.86% gain, likely buoyed by the day's biggest regulatory headline: Ripple's final OCC approval for a national trust bank charter. That approval places Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin under direct federal oversight — a meaningful step that distinguishes Ripple from most crypto firms still operating in regulatory gray areas.

Zcash's 2.35% gain stood out on a flat-to-down day. A co-founder's proposal to end the project's grants program — pointing to a $125 million treasury as justification — drew fresh attention to ZEC's balance sheet and prompted speculation about what the project might do with those reserves.

Ethereum developers also patched a critical bug in the Glamsterdam upgrade that could have incorrectly routed staking deposits to block builders. The fix was applied before any funds were affected, but the episode is a reminder that protocol upgrades carry real technical risk even when they proceed without incident.
worthKnowing: Ripple received final OCC approval for a national trust bank charter, bringing its RLUSD stablecoin under federal oversight — the first stablecoin issued by a crypto-native firm to reach this regulatory milestone.
Ethereum developers patched a critical bug in the Glamsterdam upgrade that could have sent staking deposits to block builders rather than validators; no funds were lost.

Hyperliquid announced that Payward — Kraken's parent company — will become the first CFTC-regulated entity to deploy as a HIP-3 validator on the Hyperliquid network, adding institutional backing to the protocol.
